convention: All maps are equirectangular (plate carree) 2:1. x=0 is longitude -180 deg (180W), x increases EASTWARD, x=W/2 is longitude 0, x=W is +180; y=0 is +90 deg latitude (north), y=H is -90. Pixel centres: lon = -180 + 360*(x+0.5)/W, lat = 90 - 180*(y+0.5)/H. Longitudes/latitudes are planetocentric, east-positive (IAU 2015 convention as served by USGS/NASA; for retrograde rotators the same east-positive IAU convention is kept, no mirroring applied). Gas/ice giants (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune), Venus atmosphere and Earth clouds are illustrative textures with no meaningful longitude reference. Size keys: ultra=8192x4096, high=4096x2048 (2048x1024 where the source is smaller), low=1024x512 (2048x1024 for Earth). Colour maps are sRGB JPEG; specular/height/normal/rings are linear-data PNG (earth normal ultra is lossless WebP). Normal maps are OpenGL (+Y up) tangent-space. Saturn rings: RGBA strip, x = radial position inner->outer.
